Genocide studies is an academic field of study that researches genocide . Genocide became a field of study in the mid-1940s with the work of Raphael Lemkin , who coined genocide and started genocide research, and its primary subjects were the Armenian genocide and the Holocaust . [ 1 ] The Holocaust was the primary subject matter of genocide studies, starting off as a side field of Holocaust studies , and the field received an extra impetus in the 1990s, when the Bosnian genocide and Rwandan genocide occurred. [ 2 ] It is a complex field which lacks consensus on definition principles. [ 3 ]
